play.area.aspect_changed: Note: this changes the aspect ratio of the area.
play.aspect.label: Let the coach also change the proportion of the area
play.aspect.note: Off, the area keeps your screen's proportion (16:9) and only changes size or position. On, it may stretch it on one axis only, as many experienced players do: you gain reach where you lack it, but the cursor moves a bit differently horizontally and vertically.
play.area.at_min: The area width does not go below {min} mm.
play.area.capped: The area only grows as far as it fits on the tablet.
play.area.clamped: The move was trimmed so the area stays on the tablet.
play.area.no_room: There is no room on the tablet to move the area that way.
play.area.rotation_unverified: Rotation {rotation}°: this rotation is unverified, check that the move goes the expected way.
play.area.scale_mean: The aspect ratio is kept: the mean of both axes is used (×{fx} and ×{fy} → ×{f}).
play.area.shift: Area moved {dx} mm horizontally and {dy} mm vertically.
play.area.unknown: The area size is unknown; nothing is changed.
play.close.body: There are live changes that are not saved. Save them before closing? (No = go back to your previous settings)
play.close.title: Unsaved changes
play.conv.insufficient: Not enough data this round: play more of the same map.
play.conv.nothing_left: We see no more useful changes: it's a good time to stop and save.
play.conv.plateau: There is almost nothing left to gain: it's a good time to stop and save.
play.conv.start: First round: play and we'll see what to improve.
play.conv.worse: This round was worse; we'll try smaller steps.
play.data.cursor: Cursor position while observing: to see how far your pen reaches. In memory only; erased on close.
play.data.keys: Times you press your click buttons ({keys}) and no other: to match your clicks to the map. In memory only.
play.data.map: The .osu file of the map you play: to know where the circles are. It is not copied or stored.
play.data.never: Never: osu!'s memory, other keys, other windows, your name or score, or anything over the internet.
play.data.profile: Your tablet, screen, answers and last saved settings, in a file on this PC (profile.json). Delete it from Settings.
play.data.replay: Only if you pick a replay (.osr): positions, clicks, mods and hit counts. Your name, score and date are discarded.
play.data.window: The title of osu!'s window (the map name): to find the map. No other window is read.
play.detail.note: Finer = smaller zones, but you need to play more (about 300 circles for "Fine", 600 for "Very fine").
play.detail.title: Detail of the miss map
play.find.good: We see no clear problems: your aim is going well.
play.find.jitter: The cursor shakes a little when you hold still
play.find.lag: On fast jumps the cursor arrives late (≈ {mm} mm)
play.find.reach_over: In the {dir} direction your cursor travels {pct} % more than needed
play.find.reach_short: In the {dir} direction your cursor travels {pct} % less than needed
play.find.timing: Your click timing varies quite a bit (this does not depend on the tablet)
play.find.untrusted: We couldn't match your clicks to the map. Check it is the right map and that osu! is borderless full screen.
play.keys.intro: The coach only counts these buttons as clicks:
play.keys.left_click: Left click (the pen tip) is chosen with the box below.
play.keys.listening: Press the buttons you play with now. They are only read while this window is active. Press Esc or "Done" to finish.
play.keys.manual_help: Separate with commas. Examples: z, x · mouse4 · space · num1 · f
play.keys.none_seen: I saw no click with {keys}: do you use other buttons?
play.keys.pen: I click with the pen tip (not the keyboard)
play.keys.pen_note: If you leave it off, touching with the pen does not count as a click.
play.keys.title: Your click buttons
play.map.legend: Red: more misses · arrow: where your cursor went · no colour: little data
play.map.orientation: Player's view: top = top of the screen
play.map.changed: New map recognised: {name}. The analysis starts over with it.
play.map.compare_note: You changed map: the comparison with the previous round is only approximate.
play.map.lost: You changed map, but I cannot find it. Pick the .osu file by hand when you finish.
play.msg.filter_responsive: Make the cursor more responsive on fast jumps.
play.msg.filter_steady: Make the cursor steadier when you rest.
play.msg.kept: Done: settings saved to OpenTabletDriver. The previous ones were backed up in its Backup folder.
play.msg.live_only: It is live, but not saved.
play.msg.nothing_to_apply: There is no change to apply.
play.msg.nothing_to_undo: There is no change to undo.
play.msg.play_more: Not enough data: play more of the same map; nothing is changed.
play.msg.practice_zone: The problem is only in a small zone ({place}). We do not change the area for that: play that zone more.
play.msg.rejected: That change could not be applied safely.
play.msg.revert: The last try was worse: we go back to the best settings.
play.msg.scale: Adjust the area size to what you really travel.
play.msg.send_failed: OpenTabletDriver did not accept the change; the previous settings were kept.
play.msg.shift: Move the area so your pen reaches where it needs to.
play.msg.shift_local: Move the area a little because of one zone where you miss.
play.observe.title: Watching your play
play.prep.keys_unreadable: This system cannot read the click keys (Windows only), so clicks cannot be judged.
play.prep.lazer: This looks like osu!lazer: the coach is built for osu!stable and may not line up well.
play.prep.map_not_found: I can't find that map in your Songs folder. Choose the .osu file by hand.
play.prep.no_keys: No click button is chosen: add at least one under "Your click buttons".
play.prep.no_map_title: osu! is not showing a map right now (you are in the menu). Enter a map or choose the .osu file.
play.prep.osu_closed: Open osu! and load a map.
play.prep.pen_tip: You count the pen tip as a click: in OpenTabletDriver the tip must be set to left click (the usual setting). The coach cannot check this.
play.prepare.honest: What the coach sees: where your cursor is and ONLY your click buttons ({keys}). It does not read osu!'s memory: hits and misses are worked out by comparing your clicks with the map. For exact data, pick the replay (.osr) that osu! saves yourself: only cursor positions, clicks, mods and hit counts are used from it (never your name or score). Nothing leaves your PC.
play.prepare.intro: Play a map with osu! open and the coach will tell you, in plain words, where you miss and what to change on your tablet. It repeats until there is nothing left to gain.
play.prepare.map_missing: I don't know which map you'll play yet
play.prepare.map_unreadable: That .osu file could not be read.
play.prepare.minimap: Show a small map in a corner of the screen while I play
play.prepare.minimap_note: It is not visible in exclusive full screen; use borderless or windowed mode.
play.prepare.options: What data is used (and what is not)
play.progress.title: Progress
play.rounds.all: See all rounds ({n}) and what was tried in each
play.rounds.kind.manual: You changed the area by hand.
play.rounds.kind.probe: A small change of the area was tried.
play.rounds.kind.revert: Went back to the settings of the best round.
play.rounds.nodata: The clicks could not be matched to the map, so it does not count.
play.rounds.streak: The last {n} rounds did not improve.
play.prop.local: It is because of this zone: {place}. The move is small because that zone is only part of the play.
play.prop.revert: Go back to the settings of round {round}.
play.prop.shift: Move the area {dx} mm horizontally and {dy} mm vertically (in your view of the screen).
play.replay.check: The coach matched the real game on {pct} % of the objects ({n} compared).
play.replay.check_good: You can trust what it infers.
play.replay.check_weak: The match is weak: use the replay as the round to tune with exact data.
play.replay.no_map: I need to know the map first: open osu! with the map or choose its .osu file.
play.replay.no_overlap: The replay does not match that round, so it cannot be compared.
play.replay.nothing_to_check: First play a round with the coach, then compare it with its replay.
play.replay.other_map: Note: that replay seems to be of another version of the map; the report may not be reliable.
play.replay.unreadable: I couldn't read that replay. It must be an osu!standard .osr file.
play.replay.used: This round was computed from the game's replay: exact positions and clicks, nothing estimated.
play.report.live_note: It is applied live in OpenTabletDriver, but NOT saved until you press "Save these settings".
play.report.title: What we saw
play.restore.confirm: Go back to the settings you started with and clear the round progress?
play.tech.alignment: Alignment: quality {quality} · {matched} matched clicks · speed ×{scale} · {flip} · offset {offset} ms · spread {spread} ms
play.tech.reach: Reach: gain x {gx}, y {gy} · bias x {bx} mm, y {by} mm · {n} points
play.title: Play Coach
play.warn.align_low: The clicks don't line up well with the map (quality {quality}); don't trust this report. Check the map, the speed (DT/HT) and that osu! uses borderless full screen.
play.warn.analysis_failed: This play could not be analyzed.
play.warn.few_matched: Only {n} matched clicks: play more for a solid report.
play.warn.not_enough: There are still too few clicks or data to judge the play.
play.msg.probe: A small trial with the area.
play.msg.probe_back: Put the area back as it was before the trial.
play.probe.title: The trial of the previous round
play.probe.try: We try to {what}; if it does not help, we put it back.
play.probe.why: What we saw is not enough to be sure, so we make a small trial and the next round will tell whether it helps.
play.probe.from_base: Counted from your area before the previous trial, which is put back in the same step.
play.probe.back: The trial did not improve your round and there is nothing sensible left to try: the area goes back as it was.
play.probe.kept: We tried to {what}: your round improved, so we keep it.
play.probe.reverted: We tried to {what}: your round did not improve, so we put it back.
play.probe.unclear: We tried to {what}: there is no earlier round to compare with, so it stays as it is.
play.probe.skip_back: We do not try the next change, but the area went back to how it was before the trial that did not help.
play.area.title: Your area
play.area.after: With the proposed change: {w} × {h} mm, centre {x} / {y} mm
play.area.since: Since you opened the coach (before → now):
play.area.otd_note: These are the same numbers you see in OpenTabletDriver (Width, Height, X, Y).
play.manual.title: Adjust the area by hand
play.manual.intro: Each button changes the area a little, live: the size by 2 %, the position by 0.5 mm. Directions are those of your screen: "Left" is the left of the screen even when the tablet is turned. Nothing is saved until you press "Save these settings"; "Undo" takes it back step by step.
play.manual.free_hint: To change only the width or only the height, turn on "Let the coach change the area's proportion too".
play.manual.no_room: There is no room on the tablet for that change.
play.manual.not_now: That cannot be done right now.
play.manual.needs_free: Turn on the free proportion to change one axis only.
play.smooth.title: Smoothing
play.smooth.intro: These filters are switched off in your OpenTabletDriver. You can try them: they smooth the cursor but add a little delay. You decide whether to keep them.
play.smooth.players: osu! players use them in their own way: many use none and others add a little. More smoothing means a calmer cursor, but also more delay.
play.smooth.not_installed_hint: Filters that are not installed are added from OpenTabletDriver (Plugins menu, Plugin Manager). This assistant never installs anything.
play.smooth.already_on_row: {name}: was already on in your OpenTabletDriver.
play.smooth.trying_note: You are trying it: play a round with it and we will tell you whether it went better, the same or worse.
play.smooth.decided_note: You keep it on; it is saved with "Save these settings".
play.smooth.save_note: Whatever is on when you press "Save these settings" is what gets saved. The coach never switches a filter on or off by itself; it only tunes the values of the ones that are on.
play.smooth.on: {name} switched on to try it (live, not saved).
play.smooth.off: {name} switched off again, as you had it.
play.smooth.kept: {name} stays on; it will be saved with "Save these settings".
play.smooth.own_values: The values you already had in that filter are used.
play.smooth.not_installed: {name} is not installed in your OpenTabletDriver.
play.smooth.verdict.title: With the smoothing
play.smooth.verdict.better: With {name}, this round went better than the last one without it.
play.smooth.verdict.same: With {name}, this round went the same as the last one without it: the difference is within what changes from one round to the next.
play.smooth.verdict.worse: With {name}, this round went worse than the last one without it.
play.smooth.verdict.unclear: With {name} there is not enough data to compare it with a round without it.
play.smooth.verdict.no_base: With {name} there is no round without it to compare with (you switched it on before the first round).
play.smooth.verdict.decide: Notice how it feels as well. You decide whether to keep it.
play.smooth.what.radial_tablet: Lets the tip move freely on big movements and only smooths very small ones (within a radius of a few tenths of a millimetre on the tablet).
play.smooth.feel.radial_tablet: A steadier cursor when you hold still and on short strokes; on jumps you hardly notice it.
play.smooth.what.radial_screen: The same as Radial Follow on the tablet, but the radius is measured in screen pixels.
play.smooth.feel.radial_screen: A steadier cursor on small movements; the effect on screen does not change when you resize the area.
play.smooth.what.hawku: Averages the position over a few milliseconds (its "latency"), so every movement comes out smoother.
play.smooth.feel.hawku: Smoother on slow strokes and less shaking; in exchange the cursor trails a little on fast jumps.
play.smooth.what.noise: Ignores tiny movements while the tip is almost still, averaging the last positions.
play.smooth.feel.noise: A stiller cursor when you do not move; very small movements may feel a bit sticky.
play.smooth.what.antichatter: Smooths more the slower or smaller the movement is, and very little on fast ones.
play.smooth.feel.antichatter: Less shaking when you hold still or move slowly; on fast jumps you notice it little.
play.smooth.what.resampler: Works out the cursor position more times per second than the tablet sends, so it looks smoother on fast screens.
play.smooth.feel.resampler: Smoother motion on screen; adds a few milliseconds of delay.
play.smooth.what.other: Another smoothing filter of your installation: it calms the cursor in exchange for some delay.
play.smooth.feel.other: Play a round with it and compare how it feels.
